title: Rome Conquers Greece
objective: After this level you can explain how Rome took Greece and adopted its culture.
summary: Rome ended Macedonia’s kingdom at Pydna in 168 BCE and destroyed Corinth in 146 BCE, enslaving its people, but Greek culture won over the Romans.

cards.headline: A Roman general shipped Greek masterpieces home: break one, and you replace it.
cards.body: He had no idea what he’d taken. Other Romans soon fell for Greek art.

cards.headline: Pydna, 168 BCE
cards.body: Level 87’s Antigonid kingdom ended at Pydna in 168 BCE, when Rome defeated King Perseus of Macedonia. Afterward, 1,000 leading Achaeans were deported to Rome as hostages. One of them, Polybius, would explain the whole thing to the Greeks.

cards.headline: The hostage historian
cards.body: In Rome, Polybius became a friend of the general Scipio Aemilianus. He wrote his Histories, in Greek, to explain how the Romans had brought nearly the whole inhabited world under their rule in under 53 years. A Greek hostage, telling Greeks how they’d lost.

cards.context: That’s Level 1’s finish line. Most of Corinth’s men were killed and its women and children were enslaved. The general Mummius shipped the city’s art to Rome, warning the shippers that anything lost or damaged would have to be replaced with work of equal value. As if you could order another Greek masterpiece.

cards.headline: Captive Greece
cards.body: Rome won the wars. Greece won the Romans. The poet Horace put it in one line: captive Greece took her fierce conqueror captive and brought the arts to rustic Latium.

questions.prompt: Which Roman victory in 168 BCE ended Macedonia’s Antigonid kingdom?

options.label: Chaeronea
options.rationale: That was Philip’s win in 338 BCE.

options.label: Ipsus
options.rationale: That was the Successors’ battle in 301 BCE.

options.label: Gaugamela
options.rationale: That was Alexander’s win over Persia.

questions.explanation: At Pydna in 168 BCE, Rome defeated King Perseus and ended the Antigonid kingdom.

questions.prompt: What did Horace mean by ’captive Greece took her fierce conqueror captive’?

options.label: Conquered Greece won Rome over with its arts
Greeks took Roman hostages in revenge
options.rationale: The hostages went the other way.

options.label: Rome gave Greece back its freedom

questions.explanation: Rome conquered Greece, but Greek arts and culture won over the Romans.

questions.prompt: Level 1 ends Greek independence with Corinth in 146 BCE. What happened to Corinth’s people?

options.label: Most men were killed; women and children were enslaved
They sailed west to found Syracuse

questions.explanation: When Rome destroyed Corinth, most men were killed and the women and children enslaved.
